frame.originDescription: The synthetic hull's frame: x from mid-LWL of the hull as built, y port, z up, the floated waterplane at z = 0.

sideForce.source: Clarke, Gedling & Hine (1983), 'The application of manoeuvring criteria in hull design using linear theory', Trans. RINA 125: Y'v = −π(T/L)²(1 + 0.40·Cb·B/T), N'v = −π(T/L)²(0.5 + 2.4·T/L), as reproduced in a Mathcad worksheet on ptcusercommunity.com (retrieved 2026-11-06); the paper was not checked. A regression on ships, applied to the canoe body: an extrapolation.

loading.gyradiiBasis: estimated: each item a point mass, the mast and boom thin rods, the lightship with its own k_roll = 0.35·beam and k_pitch = k_yaw = 0.25·LOA (rules of thumb, to verify)

planing.deadriseFrom: estimated from the hull's section 20% of LWL forward of its aft end

loads.notes: Static, no safety factor, no rig pretension. Chainplates: RM30 over the chainplate base (each is the windward one on its tack). Sheets: Harken's rule at the reef wind (the main's on its triangle × (1 + roach)); the staysail's isn't estimated. Halyards aren't estimated: no rule found to cite. Rudder: the larger of the torque at stall and stalled at maxDeg, at hull speed.
